dialect.detail: Standard COBOL-85 with inline PERFORM VARYING and END-IF/END-PERFORM scope terminators; no vendor-specific extensions visible

purpose.domain_detail: Academic exercise implementing LCM (Least Common Multiple) calculation and a chicken-and-dog legs puzzle (classic combinatorics problem)
purpose.summary: This program computes the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of N user-supplied numbers, then solves a classic 'chickens and dogs' head-and-legs puzzle by brute-force iteration. It accepts head count and leg count and displays valid (chickens, dogs) combinations.

notable_features: OCCURS clause for array of 10 elements
PERFORM VARYING with inline body (COBOL-85 style)
SET statement used for flag management
Mixed variable naming styles (uppercase and lowercase identifiers)
Brute-force combinatorics loop for chicken-dog puzzle
PIC Z(5)9 for formatted numeric display
verdict.notes: The program mixes uppercase and lowercase identifiers (e.g., 'num', 'chickens', 'dogs' alongside 'A', 'B', 'K'), which is typical of student code. The LCM algorithm uses a brute-force multiple-checking approach. The chicken-dog puzzle logic has a minor logical issue with the count1 flag management. No vendor-specific extensions are present, making dialect determination uncertain beyond COBOL-85.
